svg.text: The design falls straight out of one number: hundreds of thousands of

Stream views through Kafka partitioned by video
ID; each consumer counts its videos in memory
Merge the per-partition top-K lists; the result is
exact because each video lives in exactly one
Top K most-viewed videos for the last hour, day,
view events (video_id, ts) → per-minute counts per
Naive: increment a counter row per view and ORDER BY views.
That is 800k UPDATEs/sec on hot rows, then a full sort.
Stream views into Kafka partitioned by video_id, so
every view of a video lands on the same consumer.
Each consumer counts in memory in per-minute
buckets and keeps a local top-K heap.
Windows: hour = sum of the last 60 minute-buckets
(subtract the expiring one). Results are cached;
raw events go to S3 for batch correction.
A video's full count lives in one partition, so its global rank can only come from its local
rank. The global top K ⊆ union of local top Ks.
A ring buffer of minute counts per video; for months use hourly buckets. Rolling sums
Pre-aggregate on producers (send counts per second, not individual views).
Count-Min Sketch + heap uses fixed memory and is good for trending; exact needs
A counter row per video in the DB: 800k writes/sec
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
